author: Enrique Somoza
excerpt: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.
title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available

author: Cloudforce One
excerpt: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.
title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants

author: Lai Yi Ohlsen
excerpt: An examination of global Internet disruptions observed by Cloudflare Radar during the third quarter of 2026. This review analyzes how power failures, natural disasters, and government shutdowns impacted network connectivity and traffic.
title: What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026

author: Dan Jones
excerpt: We are launching a PHP Capture the Flag challenge integrated with our Bug Bounty program to test our WAF protections. Security researchers are invited to bypass our defenses and capture the flag to help make the Internet safer.
title: Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge

author: Michelle Chen
excerpt: A configuration mismatch in GLM 5.3 on Workers AI triggered an SGLang bug that exposed KV cache pages across requests. Here is how we addressed the issue.
title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang

author: Matthew Gumport
excerpt: Naive byte-range caching can waste gigabytes of origin bandwidth on small requests. We rebuilt our cache architecture in Pingora to coordinate partial fetches automatically, cutting R2 p99 latency in half.
title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning

author: Erik Engstrom
excerpt: Cloudflare's new post-quantum GeoKey Manager protects geographically fenced decryption keys from harvest now, decrypt later attacks. Learn how we redesigned our cryptography stack to support strict data sovereignty in a post-quantum world.
title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management

author: Kabin Calan
excerpt: Cloudflare has achieved South Korea's ISMS certification following an audit across 80 controls. Learn how we localized user consent flows, adapted social sign-up paths at the edge, and validated our global security program.
title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification

author: Nick Downie
excerpt: Cloudflare's web application firewall can now correlate an HTTP request with its response. Full transaction detection helps every customer find successful exploits, data exposure, and risky misconfigurations that request-only inspection can miss.
title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF

author: Kuber Nandwani
excerpt: Cloudflare has deployed default web application firewall (WAF) protections for newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities before public disclosure. The rules use request and response signals to stop exploit attempts and prevent exposed data from reaching attackers.
title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability

author: Matthew Conroy
excerpt: Almost 100,000 Commerce.com domains now give AI agents real shopping tools through WebMCP on Cloudflare. Here's how we turned it on across every store at once, while keeping each merchant in control.
title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents

author: Jeremy Hartman
excerpt: Following the discovery that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates use weak keys, Cloudflare is deploying mitigations and releasing client updates. We explain the impact, our response, and what customers and developers should do next.
title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know

author: Christoph Nakazawa
excerpt: Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.
title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust

author: Ryan Skidmore
excerpt: When our AI code reviewer's cost per run doubled, we dug into the token usage to find out why. Learn how we used prompt caching and intelligent model routing to slash our inference bill by 68% while speeding up reviews.
title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization

author: Kevin Flansburg
excerpt: Clairic is a new model from Cloudflare that is a System One extraction modeI, capable of extracting, computing, estimating, and forecasting data from unstructured inputs.
title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models

author: Kenny Johnson
excerpt: CVE-2026-88771 lets attackers run commands on NetScaler Gateway before anyone signs in. Patching takes time most teams don't have, so the sign-in decision has to move in front of the vulnerable code.
title: Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities

author: Chris Tsoukaladelis
excerpt: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly. We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.
title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots

author: Abe Carryl
excerpt: Cloudflare Gateway and Data Loss Prevention have inherited the flexibility and power of Cloudflare Workers through our full-stack integration with the Cloudflare Developer platform.
title: A fully programmable secure web gateway

author: Michael Dong
excerpt: Introducing Void: an open-source SDK, CLI, and self-hosted platform for building full-stack Vite apps and deploying them to Cloudflare.
title: Deploy with Void

author: James Balfour (OpenAI)
excerpt: How Cloudflare and OpenAI are working together to help AI find useful content, keep up with changes, and make fewer wasted requests — making the experience better for users and website owners alike.
title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone

author: Lai Yi Ohlsen
excerpt: When strikes hit Yandex data centers, many assumed Russian bot operations went dark. Cloudflare data reveals that while search crawling stopped, malicious bots simply migrated to other networks.
title: Yandex outage: Data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
